bullets: Public radio voice is a deliberate style rather than an accident — a pattern observed at teams using both BBC and NPR, and one that simplifies downstream decisions once internalized.
Reliability of pronunciation matters more than people think; its second-order effect is the part most people miss.
Listeners trust the format before they trust the content — the framing matters because it reveals which trade-offs are being made.
NPR is one of the platforms where the deliberate-style principle shows up cleanly, making it a useful reference case for how format shapes trust.
Outside of BBC-class tooling, the failure mode is harder to spot — weaker infrastructure obscures where reliability breaks down.
Reliability trade-offs cross-cut every other dimension of public-radio reporting rather than standing as an isolated concern.
Adopting one idea and running it for two weeks is the recommended starting point — the rest is iteration.
